q: Which GitHub Copilot capability is designed to handle a multi-step coding task by determining relevant files, making edits, running tools, and iterating on the result?
explanation: Agent mode is intended for agentic, multi-step development work. It can reason about the task, choose relevant context and tools, make changes, and iterate based on results rather than merely completing the current line.

q: What is the primary purpose of Model Context Protocol (MCP) when used with GitHub Copilot?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To retrain Copilot on an organization's repositories

choices.label: B
choices.text: To provide a standardized way for Copilot to access external tools and data sources

choices.label: D
choices.text: To block suggestions that match public code

explanation: MCP extends Copilot by exposing external tools and data sources through a standardized protocol, allowing agentic workflows to reach systems beyond the immediate editor or repository.

q: An organization has configured content exclusions for sensitive files. Which statement is important when developers use Agent mode in Copilot Chat?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Content exclusions are always enforced by Agent mode

choices.label: B
choices.text: Agent mode does not support content exclusion, so exclusions should not be the only protection for sensitive content

choices.label: C
choices.text: Agent mode automatically converts exclusions into .gitignore entries

choices.label: D
choices.text: Agent mode is disabled for the entire repository

explanation: GitHub documents that Agent mode in Copilot Chat in IDEs does not support content exclusion. Organizations should therefore use repository permissions and other security controls rather than treating content exclusions as a universal access-control boundary.

q: Which GitHub Copilot interfaces currently do NOT support content exclusion? Choose three.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Agent mode in Copilot Chat in IDEs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Standard inline suggestions in supported IDEs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Standard Copilot Chat where content exclusion is supported

explanation: GitHub specifically identifies Copilot CLI, Copilot cloud agent, and Agent mode in Copilot Chat in IDEs as not supporting content exclusion.

q: What is GitHub Copilot CLI primarily intended to provide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A terminal-native AI coding agent that can answer questions, work with code, and interact with GitHub

choices.label: B
choices.text: A replacement for Git version control

choices.label: D
choices.text: A local LLM that never communicates with external services

explanation: The current Copilot CLI is a terminal-native AI agent. It can answer questions, write and debug code, perform project tasks, and interact with GitHub without requiring the developer to leave the terminal.

q: Which command starts an interactive session in the current GitHub Copilot CLI?
explanation: The current standalone GitHub Copilot CLI starts an interactive session with the `copilot` command. Older material centered on `gh copilot suggest` describes the legacy GitHub CLI extension.

q: Which option allows GitHub Copilot CLI to receive a prompt non-interactively and then exit when the task is complete?
explanation: The `-p` or `--prompt` option provides a prompt directly on the command line, enabling programmatic use in terminals, scripts, and automation.

q: Which command is a documented cross-platform way to install the current GitHub Copilot CLI?
explanation: GitHub documents `npm install -g @github/copilot` as a cross-platform installation method. The npm installation requires a supported Node.js version.

q: What happens the first time Copilot CLI is started in a project directory?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It automatically commits all uncommitted changes

choices.label: B
choices.text: It can ask you to confirm that you trust the files in the current directory

choices.label: C
choices.text: It uploads the entire repository into a public knowledge base

explanation: Copilot CLI uses trusted-directory controls. On startup it can ask whether you trust the files in and below the directory from which the CLI was launched.

q: Why should a developer be cautious about granting Copilot CLI broad automatic tool permissions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It prevents Copilot from reading source files

choices.label: B
choices.text: Copilot may be able to run shell commands and modify files with the same access available to the user without asking each time

choices.label: D
choices.text: It makes all repository content public

explanation: Broad approval options can allow the agent to use tools, modify files, and execute commands without repeated confirmation. Permission scope should therefore be granted deliberately.

q: What is the purpose of plan mode in GitHub Copilot CLI?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To build and refine a structured implementation plan before writing code

explanation: Plan mode analyzes a request, can ask clarifying questions, and produces a structured implementation plan before code is written, helping the developer catch misunderstandings early.

q: What does the @ shortcut do in an interactive GitHub Copilot CLI session?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mentions files to include in context

choices.label: D
choices.text: Starts Agent mode in the IDE

explanation: In Copilot CLI, `@` is used to mention files and bring them explicitly into the session context.

q: What is the purpose of subagents in agentic Copilot workflows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To permanently replace the main agent

choices.label: B
choices.text: To offload specialized work into separate context so the main agent's context is not unnecessarily cluttered

explanation: Subagents can perform specialized tasks with their own context, helping preserve the main agent's context window while delegating work to an agent suited to the task.

q: Which scenario is the best fit for a custom subagent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A specialized security reviewer with a restricted set of tools

explanation: Custom agents can be tailored to a specialized role and given an appropriate toolset. A reviewer, for example, can be configured to analyze code without receiving tools that modify files.

q: Which statement best describes Copilot Edits compared with simple inline completion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is intended to help make coordinated edits rather than only predict the next text at the cursor

choices.label: B
choices.text: It only changes GitHub account settings

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the public-code duplication filter

explanation: Copilot Edits is aimed at making requested code changes across relevant files, while inline completion primarily predicts code at the current editing location.

q: What is the main benefit of GitHub Copilot Spaces?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They provide a curated collection of context that Copilot can use for a particular project or topic

choices.label: B
choices.text: They create isolated Git branches for every prompt

choices.label: D
choices.text: They permanently fine-tune the underlying model

explanation: Copilot Spaces let users collect relevant sources and instructions so conversations can be grounded in context for a particular task, project, or subject.

q: Which types of sources can be added to a Copilot Space? Choose three.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only content already included in the model's training data

explanation: Spaces can include GitHub repositories/files, links to GitHub issues and pull requests, uploaded files, and free-text material to provide useful context.

q: When an entire repository is attached to a Copilot Space, how is it generally used as context?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The entire repository is inserted into every prompt

choices.label: B
choices.text: Copilot searches the repository and retrieves content relevant to the question

choices.label: C
choices.text: The repository is fine-tuned into a new model

explanation: Attaching a repository does not mean every file is loaded into each prompt. Copilot retrieves relevant content from the repository based on the user's question.

q: What is a repository-wide custom instructions file commonly used by GitHub Copilot?
explanation: `.github/copilot-instructions.md` can contain repository-wide natural-language guidance that helps Copilot follow project conventions and expectations.

q: What is the purpose of path-specific custom instruction files?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To apply different Copilot guidance to particular files or directories

explanation: Path-specific instructions allow teams to provide guidance that applies only to matching files or directories, which is useful when different parts of a repository follow different conventions.

q: In a path-specific `*.instructions.md` file, what is the purpose of the `applyTo` frontmatter field?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It uses glob patterns to identify which files or directories the instructions apply to

choices.label: B
choices.text: It specifies the Copilot subscription plan

choices.label: C
choices.text: It chooses the foundation model used for training

explanation: The `applyTo` field uses glob patterns to scope instructions to relevant files, such as TypeScript files or a particular application directory.

q: Why should custom instructions generally be clear and concise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Long or vague instructions can consume useful context and may be followed less reliably

choices.label: B
choices.text: GitHub charges per character in instruction files

choices.label: C
choices.text: Instruction files cannot contain natural language

choices.label: D
choices.text: Copilot automatically deletes instructions longer than one line

explanation: Copilot has finite context and non-deterministic behavior. Clear, specific instructions reduce ambiguity and avoid wasting context on irrelevant guidance.

q: What is a prompt file useful for in GitHub Copilot workflows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reusing a well-defined prompt so similar tasks can be performed consistently

explanation: Reusable prompt files help standardize frequently repeated interactions, preserving useful task instructions instead of requiring developers to recreate the same prompt each time.

q: Which statement best describes GitHub Copilot code review?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It reviews code changes and can provide comments and suggested fixes

choices.label: B
choices.text: It automatically approves every pull request it reviews

explanation: Copilot code review analyzes changes and provides feedback, often including suggested changes that developers can apply.

q: What type of pull request review does Copilot code review leave on GitHub?
explanation: Copilot code review leaves a Comment review. It does not submit Approve or Request changes reviews.

q: Does a Copilot code review satisfy a branch rule requiring an approving pull request review?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, but only on private repositories

choices.label: C
choices.text: No; Copilot's review does not count as a required approval

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only if the repository has no human contributors

explanation: Copilot code review provides comments rather than an approving review, so it does not count toward required approvals and does not replace human approval requirements.

q: After pushing substantial new changes to a pull request that Copilot already reviewed, what may be necessary?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Request a re-review unless automatic review of new pushes is configured

explanation: Copilot does not necessarily re-review later pushes automatically. A developer can request a re-review, or the repository can be configured to review new pushes automatically.

q: What does the 'Fix with Copilot' workflow allow a developer to do from eligible Copilot code-review feedback?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delegate implementation of the suggested fix to Copilot

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mark the Copilot review as a legally required approval

choices.label: C
choices.text: Retrain the model using the pull request

explanation: Eligible review comments can be handed to Copilot so an agent can implement the requested fix, after which the resulting changes still need to be reviewed.

q: Which statement best describes automatic Copilot code review?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can be configured to trigger reviews automatically at selected points in the pull request lifecycle

choices.label: B
choices.text: It automatically merges every pull request that passes review

choices.label: D
choices.text: It only runs when a developer types /fix

explanation: Repositories and organizations can configure automatic Copilot reviews so feedback is generated without manually requesting Copilot on every eligible pull request.

q: Which feature predicts likely subsequent edits based on the changes a developer is making, rather than only completing text at the current cursor position?
explanation: Next edit suggestions anticipate where and how the developer is likely to edit next, extending assistance beyond ordinary inline completion at the current cursor.

q: For a Copilot Business or Enterprise user, what may be required before next edit suggestions can be used when the feature is governed as an editor preview?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The providing organization or enterprise must enable the relevant Editor preview features policy

choices.label: D
choices.text: The user must own the organization

explanation: Managed Copilot plans can control preview functionality through policy. GitHub documents the Editor preview features setting as relevant to next edit suggestions.

q: Which statement best distinguishes Copilot coding assistance from Copilot code review?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coding assistance helps create or modify code, while code review analyzes changes and provides review feedback

choices.label: B
choices.text: Code review is only for billing administrators

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coding assistance cannot use repository context

explanation: Coding assistance focuses on helping produce and modify code, whereas Copilot code review evaluates code changes and surfaces potential issues or improvements.

q: A developer wants Copilot to use an external issue tracker during an agentic workflow. Which capability is most directly relevant?
explanation: MCP can expose external services such as issue trackers to Copilot as tools or data sources, allowing an agent to incorporate them into a workflow.

q: An enterprise does not want developers connecting arbitrary MCP servers to Copilot. What type of control should administrators examine?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The organization's or enterprise's Copilot MCP policy

explanation: MCP availability can be governed through Copilot policy for organizations and enterprises. MCP is an extension point with security implications and should be managed accordingly.

q: Why can MCP integrations increase the security impact of an agentic Copilot session?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They can give Copilot access to additional external tools, systems, and data

choices.label: B
choices.text: They make all LLM output deterministic

choices.label: C
choices.text: They remove the need for authentication

choices.label: D
choices.text: They prevent the agent from using tools

explanation: MCP expands what an agent can reach and do. Administrators and developers should therefore consider the trustworthiness, permissions, and data exposure associated with each MCP server.

q: A developer asks Copilot to implement an issue and Copilot creates changes on a branch and opens a pull request. Which principle still applies?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The generated changes should be reviewed and validated before merging

choices.label: B
choices.text: Agent-created pull requests are automatically trustworthy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human review is prohibited for agent-created work

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pull request bypasses normal repository controls

explanation: Agentic automation does not remove the need for validation. Copilot's output should be reviewed, tested, and handled through normal repository controls.

q: What is an Agent Session in GitHub Copilot primarily used for?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tracking and interacting with an ongoing agentic task

choices.label: B
choices.text: Storing a permanent copy of the foundation model

explanation: Agent sessions provide a way to observe and interact with agentic work, including monitoring progress and steering the agent while a task is underway.

q: While an agent session is running, what is a useful way to correct or narrow the agent's direction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Steer the session with additional instructions

explanation: Agentic workflows are steerable. Additional instructions can redirect or refine the work without requiring the user to discard the entire task.

q: Which task is better suited to ordinary inline suggestions than to an autonomous agentic workflow?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Completing a small function body while the developer is typing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Implementing a feature across many files and running tests

choices.label: C
choices.text: Investigating a failing build and iterating on fixes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delegating an issue that requires multiple coordinated changes

explanation: Inline suggestions are efficient for local, immediate completions. Multi-file, iterative tasks are better candidates for agentic capabilities.

q: Which task is best suited to Agent mode rather than a single inline completion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Renaming one local variable as you type

choices.label: B
choices.text: Implementing a feature that requires edits in several files and running tests to validate the result

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accepting the next word of a suggestion

explanation: Agent mode is designed for multi-step tasks where Copilot must plan, edit multiple locations, use tools, and react to test or command output.

q: Which of the following is the best reason to use a reusable prompt file?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A team repeatedly performs the same kind of task and wants consistent instructions

choices.label: B
choices.text: A team wants to bypass access controls

choices.label: C
choices.text: A developer wants to hide code from Git

choices.label: D
choices.text: An administrator wants to assign Copilot seats

explanation: Prompt files are useful when a task or workflow is repeated. They make successful prompt structure reusable and reduce variation between repeated requests.

q: What is a key difference between providing context and giving instructions to Copilot?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Context supplies relevant information; instructions describe how Copilot should approach or format the task

choices.label: B
choices.text: Context and instructions are always identical

choices.label: C
choices.text: Instructions can only contain source code

explanation: Context grounds Copilot with relevant material, while instructions guide behavior, constraints, conventions, or expected output. Effective prompts often use both.

q: A developer gives Copilot a large number of unrelated files while asking about one function. What is a likely consequence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Irrelevant context can compete with useful context and reduce response quality

explanation: More context is not automatically better. Relevant, targeted context helps the model focus, while unrelated material can consume context capacity and distract from the task.

q: Which workflow best demonstrates responsible use of Copilot for legacy-code modernization?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ask Copilot for modernization changes, review the proposed changes, run tests, and validate behavior

choices.label: B
choices.text: Accept every generated migration without testing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Assume newer syntax guarantees equivalent behavior

explanation: Copilot can accelerate modernization, but generated migrations can alter behavior or introduce errors. Review and testing remain necessary.

q: How can Copilot help when creating tests for existing code? Choose three.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Generate unit or integration test scaffolding

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prove the implementation has no defects

explanation: Copilot can accelerate test creation by generating tests, surfacing edge cases, and suggesting assertions, but it cannot guarantee complete coverage or defect-free code.

q: A Copilot-generated security fix appears plausible. What is the appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Validate the change with testing, review, and appropriate security tooling or guidance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Merge immediately because Copilot identified it as a security fix

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assume the generated code cannot introduce a new vulnerability

explanation: Copilot can suggest security improvements, but generated output remains probabilistic and must be independently reviewed and validated.

q: Which statement about preview features and the GH-300 exam is most accurate according to Microsoft's study guide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The exam can never contain preview features

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most questions focus on generally available features, but commonly used preview features may appear

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every question is about preview functionality

choices.label: D
choices.text: Preview features are tested only in renewal assessments

explanation: Microsoft states that most exam questions cover generally available features, while commonly used preview features may also appear.

q: Which current GH-300 objective explicitly appears in the August 7, 2026 study guide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use Agent Mode, Copilot Edits, and MCP to streamline development and workflows

choices.label: B
choices.text: Train a new foundation model from scratch

explanation: The August 7, 2026 objectives explicitly call out Agent Mode, Copilot Edits, and MCP, along with agent sessions and delegation to subagents.

q: Which current GH-300 objective was added to the Copilot CLI section of the August 7, 2026 skills outline?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use Copilot CLI interactively and in sessions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a GitHub Enterprise Server appliance

explanation: The updated skills outline specifically covers defining Copilot CLI, installing it, understanding key commands, using it interactively and in sessions, and using it for scripts and file management.

q: Which group of features is explicitly named in the August 7, 2026 GH-300 objectives under GitHub Copilot features and capabilities?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Spaces, Spark, pull request summaries, and customizable review standards through instruction files

choices.label: B
choices.text: GitHub Pages, Dependabot billing, and Codespaces port forwarding only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Azure Boards, Azure Pipelines, and Microsoft Teams only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Git LFS, submodules, and release assets only

explanation: The current skills outline explicitly names Spaces, Spark, pull request summaries, and customizable review standards using instruction files.

q: What is the purpose of GitHub Spark in the context of current Copilot capabilities?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To help create and iterate on applications using natural-language-driven development

choices.label: D
choices.text: To replace the Copilot public-code filter

explanation: Spark is part of GitHub's AI-assisted application-building experience and is explicitly named among the current GH-300 Copilot capabilities.

q: Which statement about organization-wide Copilot policy is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Administrators can govern feature availability, including features in IDEs and on GitHub.com

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every developer can override enforced enterprise policy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Copilot policy can only be configured in .gitignore

explanation: Current GH-300 objectives include organization-wide policy management, enabling Copilot code review policies, and managing feature availability across IDE and GitHub.com experiences.

q: What is a useful role of organization audit-log events in Copilot administration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Provide accountability for administrative and policy-related actions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Store every generated code completion verbatim

explanation: Audit logs are used to track relevant administrative events and configuration changes, supporting governance and accountability rather than storing the content of every suggestion.

q: A developer receives a plausible Copilot-generated authentication routine. What should they do before using it in production?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Review, test, and validate it against security requirements

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume it is secure because Copilot generated it

choices.label: C
choices.text: Merge it directly if it compiles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable code review to avoid conflicting feedback

explanation: Copilot output requires human review and validation, especially for security-sensitive code.

q: Which risk is most directly associated with treating generative AI output as authoritative?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hallucinated or inaccurate output can be accepted without verification

choices.label: B
choices.text: The IDE will stop compiling code

choices.label: D
choices.text: Copilot will always expose private repositories

explanation: Generative models can produce confident but incorrect output, so verification is a core responsible-use practice.

q: A team wants to reduce bias in an AI-assisted workflow. Which approach is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use diverse evaluation data and human oversight

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use the largest possible prompt regardless of relevance

explanation: Diverse evaluation and human oversight help identify and mitigate unfair or biased behavior.

q: Which statement best reflects transparency in responsible AI use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Users should understand important limitations and when AI is being used

choices.label: B
choices.text: AI output should never be reviewed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every suggestion should be accepted automatically

explanation: Transparency includes making AI use and meaningful limitations understandable to users.

q: Why is human oversight still important when Copilot can run multi-step agentic tasks?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autonomy increases the scope of possible mistakes, so results and actions still need supervision

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human review is only required for free plans

explanation: Agentic workflows can take broader actions, which makes appropriate oversight and validation more important.

q: What is the safest interpretation of a Copilot-generated explanation of unfamiliar code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Treat it as a hypothesis to verify against the code and tests

choices.label: C
choices.text: Assume it reflects the original author's intent

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use it to bypass code review

explanation: Generated explanations can be incomplete or wrong and should be checked against authoritative evidence.

q: Copilot proposes a dependency version that does not exist. What type of GenAI limitation does this illustrate?
explanation: A fabricated but plausible dependency is an example of hallucination.

q: Which action best protects intellectual property when Copilot returns code similar to public code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use public-code matching/reference information and review licensing implications

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume all generated code is license-free

explanation: Public-code controls and references help developers evaluate matching code and licensing implications.

q: A generated unit test passes, but it only tests the happy path. What should the developer do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add meaningful edge and failure cases based on requirements

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assume passing means coverage is complete

explanation: Generated tests can miss important cases; developers remain responsible for adequate test design.

q: Which principle is most relevant when ensuring an AI-assisted feature works for people with different abilities?
explanation: Inclusiveness focuses on designing systems that empower and accommodate people with diverse needs.

q: A developer wants Copilot to focus on one specific file that is not currently open. What should they do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Explicitly add or reference that file as context

explanation: Explicitly supplying relevant context is more reliable than expecting Copilot to infer an unopened file.

q: Why can keeping unrelated files open sometimes reduce the usefulness of automatically gathered context?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Irrelevant context can compete with information relevant to the task

choices.label: B
choices.text: Copilot permanently trains on open tabs

explanation: Context should be relevant and focused; unrelated material can distract the model.

q: Which is the best prompt for generating a function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Implement parseDate(input) in TypeScript; return null for invalid ISO dates and include tests for leap years

explanation: A specific goal, language, behavior, constraints, and success criteria produce better results.

q: What is the main value of next edit suggestions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They anticipate likely edits beyond the current cursor based on recent changes

explanation: Next edit suggestions predict likely subsequent edits, extending assistance beyond ordinary completion.

q: A developer wants to accept only part of an inline suggestion. What capability is relevant?
explanation: Supported editors allow developers to accept portions of suggestions rather than the entire completion.

q: Which context is most useful when asking Copilot to fix a failing function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The function, relevant error output, and related tests

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every file in every repository you own

explanation: Relevant code, errors, and tests provide strong grounding for a debugging request.

q: A Copilot response keeps referring to a previous task in the same chat. What is a reasonable remedy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Start a fresh conversation or remove stale context

explanation: Stale conversation history can bias responses toward an earlier task.

q: What is the benefit of giving Copilot examples of desired input and output?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They clarify expected behavior and format

explanation: Examples reduce ambiguity and are a form of few-shot prompting.

q: Which prompt-engineering approach breaks a complex task into smaller, verifiable requests?
explanation: Decomposing a complex task can improve focus and make intermediate results easier to verify.

q: A developer asks Copilot to 'optimize this' without identifying goals. Why is the prompt weak?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Optimization is ambiguous without criteria such as speed, memory, readability, or complexity

explanation: Clear success criteria tell Copilot what kind of optimization is actually desired.

q: Agent mode runs tests after editing code and sees a failure. What behavior makes it agentic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can use the failure as feedback and iterate on the implementation

choices.label: B
choices.text: It must stop after the first edit

explanation: Agentic workflows can take actions, inspect results, and iterate toward the goal.

q: Which task is most appropriate to delegate to a coding agent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A well-scoped issue requiring coordinated code changes and tests

explanation: Coding agents are suited to scoped software tasks that can be reviewed through normal development workflows.

q: What should a developer do when an agent proposes a shell command with destructive potential?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inspect the command and deny or modify the action if it is unsafe

choices.label: B
choices.text: Approve it because the agent generated it

explanation: Tool actions should be reviewed according to their impact and granted only appropriate permissions.

q: Why are well-scoped tasks generally better for coding agents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clear boundaries improve planning, verification, and review

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scope has no effect on agent behavior

explanation: Specific goals and boundaries make agentic work easier to execute and validate.

q: An agent has misunderstood a requirement midway through a task. What is preferable to silently accepting the result?
explanation: Agent sessions can be steered with additional instructions when the work is heading in the wrong direction.

q: What is a practical advantage of delegating specialized investigation to a subagent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It can isolate specialized context and return focused findings to the main workflow

choices.label: C
choices.text: It removes the need for review

explanation: Subagents can handle focused tasks without overloading the main agent's context.

q: A custom agent is intended only to review code. What is a sensible design choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Give it only the tools needed for read/review work

choices.label: B
choices.text: Give it unrestricted write and deployment access

explanation: Least-privilege tool access reduces unnecessary risk.

q: What is the difference between agentic execution and ordinary chat advice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Agentic execution can take tool-driven actions and iterate, while ordinary chat may only return guidance

explanation: Agents can perform actions through tools, not merely describe what a developer could do.

q: Why should agent-generated changes still pass CI?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Automated validation helps detect regressions and errors in generated changes

choices.label: C
choices.text: CI only applies to human code

choices.label: D
choices.text: Agent output is guaranteed to compile

q: An agent creates a pull request for an assigned issue. Who remains responsible for deciding whether the changes are acceptable?

q: What does an MCP server expose to an AI client such as Copilot?

choices.text: Trust, permissions, data access, and the actions the server can perform

q: A Copilot agent needs current information from an internal service that is not part of the repository. What can MCP provide?

q: Which statement about MCP and repository permissions is correct?

choices.label: B
choices.text: MCP automatically grants access to every repository

q: An MCP tool can create tickets in an external system. What new capability does that give an agent?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ability to retrain the LLM

choices.label: C
choices.text: The ability to bypass all policy

q: Why might an enterprise restrict which MCP servers are allowed?

choices.label: B
choices.text: It never leaves the local machine

q: Which is NOT the purpose of MCP?

choices.text: Fine-tuning the underlying Copilot model on every connected service

choices.label: D
choices.text: Allowing agent access to supported capabilities

q: A team connects a production database through an MCP server. What is the most important initial design concern?

choices.text: Restrict permissions and prefer safe, narrowly scoped operations

choices.label: B

q: Which command can be used in Copilot CLI to request a review of code changes?

q: Which statement about current Copilot CLI and older `gh copilot` material is most accurate?

q: A team has a standard pull-request review checklist it wants Copilot to consider. Which mechanism is directly relevant?

q: Which information should NOT be placed casually into custom instructions or prompts?
